Inglewood, California
  February 9, 2021

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
February 9, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:01 p.m.

The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla, and Faulk;
  and
  Absent:  Council Member Morales (arrived at 1:04 p.m.)

City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on
Closed Session Item Nos. CS-1 and CS-2.

Gil Mathieu, District 4, requested a brief oral report regarding CS-1, Closed Session
Workers Compensation Claim with Mariano Salcedo.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:07 p.m. for Closed Session Item
Nos. CS-1 and CS-2.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
hour of 2:01 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
presence of a quorum as follows:

  Chairman Butts/Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.

follows:
  Aisha Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
item on the Agendas, other than the public hearing.

  1
   Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on Warrants and Bills.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member/ Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  February 4, 2021, in the amount of $4,979,640.30 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  HEARING HELD – RESOLUTION NOS. 21-52, 21-53, 21-54, 21-55, 21-56, 21-57,
  21-58, 21-59, 21-60, 21-61, AND 21-62 RESCINDED; RESOLUTION NOS. 21-52
  (A), 21-56 (A), 21-57(A), 21-58 (A), 21-59(A), 21-60(A), AND 21-61(A) ADOPTED -
  RESOLUTIONS OF NECESSITY TO ACQUIRE PROPERTY FOR THE
  INGLEWOOD BASKETBALL AND ENTERTAINMENT CENTER (“IBEC”)
  PROJECT. The City Clerk announced that the next scheduled matter was a Resolutions
  of Necessity Hearing to consider the rescission of previously adopted Resolutions of
  Necessity, and the adoption of Resolutions of Necessity to acquire property in the city of
  Inglewood for the Inglewood Basketball and Entertainment Center (“IBEC”) Project, and
  that notices were given in the time, form and manner as required by law, an affidavit was
  on file, and communications were received.

  The City Clerk, Aisha Thompson, received communications via email from Hossein
  Razaghpanah, who opposed the Resolutions of Necessity. She also stated that
  Declarations of Mailing were received from Savine Investments, LLC c/o Daniel
  Saparzadeh Managing Member; Church’s Chicken; Danfar PCH LLC & Afifi Family
  Revocable Trust; Susie Quon; Edward Y. Michino & James Masataka Michino; Vital
  Proteins, LLC; Dev Anan Bhalla and Roopa Bhalla; and Big G’s Auto, who also opposed
  the Resolutions of Necessity.

  Mayor Butts ordered the communications received and filed.

  Christopher Jackson, Economic and Community Development Director, presented a staff
  report dated February 9, 2021.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on the matter.

  Farian Afifi, Attorney representing the owners of the properties located at 10004 S.
  Prairie Avenue, 10022 S. Prairie Avenue, and the vacant lot adjoining the two, spoke
  regarding their clients’ objection to the Resolutions of Necessity. He stated his clients do
  not feel the project is most compatible with the greatest public good, and they do not
  believe the City Council considered what is good for the public. Lastly, he expressed his
  clients do not think their properties are necessary for the project. He also spoke regarding
  Code of Civil Procedure (CCP) Section 1240.030.

  Daniel Saparzadeh, managing member of Sabine Investments LLC, owns and controls
  the property located at 10004 S. Prairie Avenue and the adjacent lot. Mr. Saparzadeh
  informed the City Council that he invested his life savings into the City, and despite the
  many challenges the City faced, they remained hopeful that the future would be bright.
  Lastly, Mr. Saparzadeh shared his beliefs on why the City of Inglewood was chosen for
  the IBEC Project.

  Council Member Morales left the dais at 2:23 p.m.

  Kevin Brogan, Counsel for the family who owns 3915 W. 102nd Street, objected to the
  Resolutions of Necessity, stating the proposed acquisition of his client’s property is not

  2
   for public use, and it violates the Code of Civil Procedure Section 1240.010 and also
  stating reference to the Norm’s Slauson Case. Lastly, he stated it is an inappropriate use
  of Code of Civil Procedure Section 1240.12a.

  Council Member Morales returned to the dais at 2:24 p.m.

  Dean Dennis, Counsel for Devin Rupabala and Susie Quan (property parcel numbers
  ending in 035 and 033), objected to the Resolutions of Necessity and is willing to
  challenge the right to take the property based on the fact that there is no Public use for the
  project. Mr. Dennis stated that he would argue in court that the hearing held on February
  9, 2021, is a pretext for transferring private property to another private owner for a
  private development that is not permitted under California's Constitution.

  Neil Brauer, representative for Sabine Investments, who owns 10004 S. Prairie Avenue,
  spoke to reiterate his objection to the Resolutions of Necessity. He referred to
  Government Code Section 7267.2, stating his belief that the offer received does not
  satisfy the provisions of the Government Code, and the basis for the evaluation was
  unclear. Mr. Brauer raised concerns regarding SoFi Stadium and other venues nearby,
  citing traffic in the community. He also objected to the City's offer of $200 per square
  foot, and intended to contest in the event of any combination proceedings brought on this
  property.

  Farhan Yazinian, owner of Sabine Investment LLC, wanted to know why Mr. Ballmer
  couldn't use the Forum to build a stadium instead of taking people's property.

  Dev Bhalla, warehouse owner, spoke concerning his loyalty to the City of Inglewood,
  and he looked forward to starting a family business. He further stated he has been a
  resident of Inglewood for over 30 years and thought he would reap the benefits of being
  committed to the City. He reiterated his objections to the project because he felt the offers
  that were made were unfair to the property owners. Mr. Bhalla spoke about the square
  footage of the appraisals being off and wanted to make the City Council aware. Lastly, he
  asked to be treated fairly and requested that the City Council do what is right.

Gil Mathieu, District 4, spoke in agreement with Mr. Bhalla about eminent domain
  proceedings. Mr. Mathieu offered his advice saying, "this is Corporate America, and the
  little man doesn't count." He also spoke concerning the selling of the Forum and the City
  Council's involvement.

  Brenda Aguilar, Outside Counsel, spoke regarding the appraisals done on the properties
  in question for eminent domain. She gave a brief oral report regarding the inspections of
  the properties in question and the property owners' refusal to allow the appraiser onto the
  properties. Finally, she addressed the City of Inglewood being a Charter City, and
  pursuant to the Inglewood Charter Article 3, Section 4, the City can use eminent domain
  to acquire property.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the City Council does hereby: 1) Rescind previously adopted Resolutions of
  Necessity (“RONs”) adopted for APN Nos. 4032-001-039 (P1), 4032-001-005 (P3),
  4032-001-006 (P4), 4032-001-033 (P5), 4032-001-048 (P6), 4032-008-001 (P7), and
  4032-007-035 (P12); 2) Make the required findings pursuant to Code of Civil Procedures
  Section 1240.030, and 3) Adopt the following Resolutions of Necessity authorizing and
  directing the City’s attorneys to prepare, commence, and file proceedings in eminent
  domain for the purpose of acquiring the private parcels that are needed for the
  development of the proposed IBEC Project: Resolution No. 21-52 (A) entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
